what_its_for: Sodium bicarbonate is a antacid used to relieve heartburn, acid indigestion, and upset stomach. It works by neutralizing excess stomach acid. It may also be used to make your urine less acidic, which can help treat certain kidney problems or urinary tract conditions.
how_to_take: If you are taking sodium bicarbonate tablets, swallow them whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). If you are using the powder form, dissolve it completely in a glass of water and drink the entire mixture. Do not take it on a completely full or completely empty stomach. Take it at least 1 to 2 hours apart from other medications, since it can affect how other drugs are absorbed.
dosing: For heartburn or upset stomach in adults, the typical dose is 325 mg to 2,000 mg (1 to 4 tablets or as directed on the label) taken up to 4 times a day. Do not take more than 200 mEq of sodium in a 24-hour period. Your doctor may prescribe a different dose depending on your condition. Always follow your doctor's instructions or the directions on the package label. Do not use for more than 2 weeks unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you are taking sodium bicarbonate on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store sodium bicarbonate at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking sodium bicarbonate with milk or other dairy products, as this can cause a condition called milk-alkali syndrome. Do not take it for longer than 2 weeks unless directed by your doctor. Avoid using it if you are on a low-sodium diet, as this medication contains a significant amount of sodium. Limit alcohol consumption, as alcohol can worsen stomach acid problems. Do not take it at the same time as other medications without checking with your pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe stomach pain or cramping, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, swelling of the hands, feet, or ankles, unusual weight gain, muscle weakness or twitching, feeling very thirsty or urinating more than usual, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your heartburn or stomach symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks of use.
when_it_works: Sodium bicarbonate works quickly, usually within 5 to 15 minutes after taking it. Relief from heartburn and acid indigestion is typically short-lasting, so you may need to take it more than once throughout the day as directed. It is not meant to be a long-term solution for ongoing stomach problems.
special_populations: Older adults should use sodium bicarbonate with caution because they may be more sensitive to its side effects, especially fluid retention and electrolyte imbalances. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using it, as the high sodium content could be a concern. Children under 12 years of age should not use sodium bicarbonate for heartburn unless directed by a doctor. People with kidney disease, high blood pressure, heart failure, or liver disease should avoid this medication or use it only under close medical supervision, as the sodium content may worsen these conditions.
